text:
sam: noticed an uptick in p99 for streaming chat after the 03:00 deploy. users report laggy responses. flamegraph + perf samples look host-heavy. snapshot: https://perf.internal/runs/7992000 :worried:

riku: which stacks are hot? small vs long requests?

sam: primarily mid-to-long requests (200-1500 tokens). perf top minutes:
````
22.1% host::parse_stream
17.4% tokenizer::unicode_fold_normalize
13.0% grpc::WriteV
11.2% kernel_selector::evaluate_candidates
7.6% kvcache::lookup_miss_path
5.8% http2::frame_pack
````

Dana: tokenizer change yesterday was the "unicode_fold" patch to collapse grapheme clusters + normalize NFKC. Did that change the prefix hashing scheme for kvcache keys?

sam: yes 1% of recent misses map to new prefix hashes. keys expanded because some emoji sequences collapsed differently, changing the first-k-token signature we use for KV lookup. kvcache hit_rate dropped from 97% -> 82% at the same timestamp.

riku: and kernel_selector::evaluate_candidates is up because we're hitting a compatibility path for sequences >1024 (compat kernels avoid quantized ops). Mixed-length batches amplify the cost since selector runs the slow branch more often.

Dana: grpc::WriteV spike could be a side-effect of larger responses from retries and extra work on host. http2 framing also increased due to fragmentation.

perf-bot: quick AB bench (master vs canary):
````
master: p95=95ms p99=180ms qps=480
canary: p95=125ms p99=260ms qps=450
canary + split_long: p95=100ms p99=190ms qps=470
````

riku: short-term mitigation options:
- enable batch split: separate long (>512) requests into their own micro-batches before kernel selection
- add a temporary kernel-override: prefer quantized kernels if batch composition is >75% short sequences
- opt-out heavy unicode_fold on hot-path for the next 1h deploy window (degrade normalization but keep keys stable)

sam: I'll push a canary with batch-split + kernel-override flags. also adding debug logging for "kernel_reason" and a small sample of batch seq_lens (1/1000 requests) to telemetry.

Dana: I'll prepare a tokenizer follow-up to keep new normalization but emit a "token_key_version" tag and a legacy-hash fallback when kvcache misses occur within a 5m window to avoid mass misses on deploy. ticket INF-2225.

riku: kvcache team: consider a rolling multi-version read window (keep last 2 key versions readable) and increase hot-shard allocation during deploys. also add eviction pacing to avoid bursts.

perf-bot: local microbench after quick canary: p99 improvement ~50ms vs canary without fixes. throughput drop negligible.

sam: long-term proposals:
- kernel_selector: make scoring batch-composition-aware (penalize fallbacks when mixed batches present; or pre-split batches before selection)
- dedicated worker lanes for long-sequence requests so they don't perturb short-request latency (experiment INF-2230)
- make tokenizer normalization backward-compatible for kvcache-key derivation or decouple prefix-key from user-visible normalization
- tune grpc WriteV coalescing thresholds to reduce syscall churn for larger streaming responses

Dana: adding monitoring alerts: kvcache.hit_rate drop >5% in 10m and kernel_selector.fallback_rate >2% should page infra oncall during deploy windows.

ops-bot: deploy canary (deploy/799201) started, will post status and AB results.

riku: thanks. reviewing canary now. if perf-bot confirms p95/p99 back near baseline, we'll rollback tokenizer opt-out and schedule the multi-version kvcache work.

sam: rolling the canary with batch-split+override. will update in 15m. cheers.
